claim: Cards accepted in urban/upmarket venues but rural and hawker spots are cash-only; most Malaysian banks add no own ATM fee; decline DCC and charge in MYR.
quote: Not all establishments in Malaysia accept cards or contactless payments, particularly in more rural areas... to avoid extra fees while withdrawing cash in Malaysia, select 'Decline/Without' Conversion or 'Charge in MYR'.

claim: Malaysian ATMs widely accept foreign Visa/Mastercard; accepting the ATM's on-screen currency conversion adds an extra fee.
quote: When withdrawing cash as a foreign visitor, if you accept the ATM's currency conversion offer, you pay an extra percentage fee.

claim: Bank cards typically charge a foreign-transaction markup on overseas spending, which Wise-type cards avoid.
quote: Guide to Malaysia credit card overseas transaction fees: Foreign transaction, dynamic currency conversion, and more.

claim: TNG eWallet supports ~20 countries/regions (incl. France, Germany); foreigners register with passport/ID, selfie verification and a WhatsApp OTP, topping up via international card.
quote: The platform supports visitors from 20 countries/regions, including Australia, Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, China, France, Germany, Hong Kong, and India... one-time password (OTP) sent to your WhatsApp.

claim: Malaysia expanded TNG eWallet access to ASEAN tourists ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026.
quote: Malaysia expands TNG eWallet access for Asean tourists ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026.

claim: Tourists can register for TNG eWallet before arrival using a foreign mobile number and passport, reloading via home-country cards.
quote: Users are able to register for their TNG eWallet account before arriving in Malaysia... reload their eWallet balance using their home country-issued credit or debit cards.

claim: Since Feb 2026 physical SIMs require passport, biometric photo and a local address, while eSIMs skip registration entirely.
quote: Since Feb 2026: Physical SIMs require original passport + biometric photo + hotel address (MCMC rules), but eSIMs skip all registration.

claim: CelcomDigi Prepaid 5G is RM25 for 40 GB; Hotlink/Maxis and U Mobile offer similar RM25 unlimited/40 GB plans.
quote: Its Prepaid 5G NX plan, priced at RM25 (about $5), includes 40 GB of high-speed data, 5G access, and unlimited local calls.

claim: Local tourist SIMs cost RM20-50 ($5-12); eSIM data plans for Malaysia typically run $10-50 depending on data and duration.
quote: tourist SIMs usually cost RM20-50 ($5-12)... The cost of eSIM data plans covering Malaysia typically ranges from $10 to $50.

claim: CelcomDigi has the strongest overall 4G/5G coverage and is the best tourist choice for Borneo, Langkawi and the Perhentians; all carriers share the DNB 5G network.
quote: CelcomDigi has the strongest overall 4G/5G coverage in Malaysia and is the best choice for tourists, especially when traveling beyond Kuala Lumpur to places like Borneo, Langkawi or the Perhentian Islands.

claim: On Borneo's Route 22 (KK-Sandakan-Sukau) service rarely dropped, but the Tip of Borneo and parts of the Kinabatangan river are patchy or have no coverage.
quote: service didn't drop out for more than a minute or two on either network. However, some places won't have coverage at all, or patchy coverage, such as Tip of Borneo and Kinabatangan River.

claim: CDC recommends routine vaccines plus Hep A, typhoid, Hep B, and case-by-case JE/rabies; P. knowlesi malaria occurs in rural forested areas with none in KL/Penang/George Town; prevent mosquito bites for dengue.
quote: Zoonotic transmission of P. knowlesi malaria occurs in rural, forested areas. No transmission occurs in Kuala Lumpur (the capital), in Penang State, on Penang Island, or in George Town.

claim: Travelers to Borneo are urged to consult a healthcare provider about malaria prevention including antimalarials; standard food/water precautions apply.
quote: those heading to Borneo are urged to consult with a healthcare provider about malaria prevention, including the potential need for antimalarial medications.

claim: Health authorities flag rising dengue, TB and malaria risk for Malaysia in 2026 and advise pre-trip vaccination consultation; dengue mosquitoes feed in daytime.
quote: Health Alert: Millions of Visitors to Malaysia in 2026 Must Get Vaccinated Rising TB, Dengue, and Malaria Risks... Dengue is a viral infection spread by mosquitoes which mainly feed during daytime hours.

claim: Belgium's FPS Foreign Affairs travel page for Malaysia covers safety and travel guidance for Belgian visitors.
quote: Travelling in Malaysia | FPS Foreign Affairs - Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation.

claim: Eat/give with the right hand, remove shoes entering homes/mosques, dress modestly; alcohol is legal but not served by Muslim-owned venues and restricted in conservative states; multicultural Malay/Chinese/Indian society.
quote: always use your right hand... Muslim-owned establishments do not serve alcohol, and in more conservative states like Kelantan and Terengganu, access is more limited.

claim: At mosques, remove shoes and dress modestly: women cover arms, legs and hair, men wear long trousers; robes are usually provided; avoid Friday midday prayers.
quote: you must dress modestly, remove your shoes... Men should wear long pants, and women should cover their arms, legs, and hair. Robes are usually provided if needed.

claim: During Ramadan avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public during daylight and dress conservatively; public displays of affection beyond hand-holding are discouraged.
quote: you should try to avoid eating, drinking, or smoking in public out of respect... Public displays of affection are not common in Malaysia.

claim: Beer costs ~RM6-13 per can in supermarkets and RM15-25 in bars/restaurants in 2026.
quote: you might pay around RM 10 to RM 15 for a can at a supermarket. At a bar or restaurant, expect to pay more, usually between RM 15 and RM 25.

claim: Budget 2026 raised alcohol excise duties by 10% from 1 Nov 2025, the first such increase since 2013.
quote: Cigarette and alcohol excise duties up from Nov 1 under Budget 2026 as govt promotes healthier living.

claim: The Eastern Sabah Security Zone covers east-coast districts (Kudat, Sandakan, Lahad Datu, Semporna, Tawau); Sipadan/Mabul/Kapalai have permanent police-military outposts and a coastal night curfew.
quote: Popular islands such as Sipadan, Mabul, and Kapalai have permanent police and military outposts... A night-time curfew remains in effect for designated coastal waters.

claim: US State Dept rates islands and maritime areas off eastern Sabah Level 2 (increased caution) while lowering mainland east Sabah to Level 1; general petty-crime caution applies.
quote: lowered its travel advisory for eastern areas of Sabah to Level 1 - Exercise Normal Precautions, though islands and maritime areas off the coast of Eastern Sabah remain at Level 2.

claim: Common Malaysia scams: taxi meter-refusal/overcharging (use Grab), fake airport Grab drivers, ATM skimming, and no-show 'budget tour'/fake-guide scams.
quote: Corrupt taxi drivers might refuse to use the meter... only get in a Grab car with a license plate matching the car you've ordered... ATM skimming involves criminals installing a tiny card reader.

claim: UK FCDO advises against all but essential travel to all islands and dive sites off the coast of eastern Sabah from Sandakan to Tawau, but not mainland Sabah.
quote: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to all islands and dive sites off the coast of eastern Sabah from Sandakan to Tawau.

claim: More countries lifted Level 3 warnings on eastern Sabah in 2025-26; no kidnap-for-ransom incident has been reported since January 2020.
quote: no kidnap-for-ransom incidents have been reported in eastern Sabah waters since January 2020.

claim: Per-person daily Malaysia budgets: shoestring RM100-160 ($22-35), mid RM175-275 ($38-60), flashpacker RM275+ ($60+); Malaysian Borneo costs 20-400% more than the peninsula.
quote: Shoestring Backpacker: 100-160 RM ($22-35 USD/day)... Malaysian Borneo costs 20-400% more than Peninsular Malaysia.

claim: Mid-range couples should budget roughly $70-120/day with ~$55/day accommodation for two; comfort travel costs more.
quote: the accommodation costs $55 per day for two people in double/twin rooms... Overall mid-range travelers... should budget $70-$120 per day.
